- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or adjust downward by 1–3% if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is trending up, model may overreact; reduce forecast slope or apply mean reversion if price deviates >2SD from 14-day moving average.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.8) and price is volatile, model often overfits recent highs; use 30-day moving average as baseline and adjust forecast downward if sentiment drops below 0.6.
- If model forecast is consistently > true outcome by 2–4% over 3–5 days, apply downward bias correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is weak or negative, model tends to overestimate; apply a 1–3% downward adjustment to the first 10 days of forecast if sentiment <0.4 for 3+ days.
- If sentiment is high and price is near support level, model may overestimate; cap forecast at 1–2% above current price if sentiment >0.8 and price is below 72.00.
